description: FINDING 1, the priority. identity/customer.py::normalize_phone strips the '+' before any country-code detection, so _INDIAN_MOBILE_RE (^[6-9]\d{9}$) matches a 10-digit foreign E.164 number and DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE='91' is prepended to an already-complete number. Reproduced live: +6591234567 -> +916591234567, +6421234567 -> +916421234567, +6689123456 -> +916689123456, +9715012345 -> +919715012345, and via the 00 branch 0065 9123 4567 -> +916591234567. The OTP reaches an unrelated Indian subscriber, the real customer can never sign in, and the WRONG identity is reserved because uniqueness is enforced on this value. Reachable from the shipped UI: src/lib/dialCodes.ts offers +65 Singapore. Fix: add a strict normaliser that branches on the explicit '+' or '00' marker BEFORE any digit-stripping and never applies the India default, then wire it at the four customer-facing phone entry points only. A SECOND independent copy of the same bug lives in the standalone customer-whatsapp-auth trigger and must be fixed in the same change, or a correctly-registered foreign customer's sign-in OTP starts going to an Indian stranger. Read .agents/tasks/phone-normalisation-fix-20261001/plan.md sections 0, 1 and 3 in full - they contain the exact design, the entry-point justification, and the complete test table.
steps: Read plan.md sections 0 (findings), 1.1-1.5 (design decisions) and 3 (test list) before writing code. Do not re-derive the design.

In amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/identity/customer.py, ADD (never modify) class MissingCountryCode(InvalidPhoneNumber) and def normalize_phone_preserving_country(raw: Any) -> str, and add both to __all__. Leave normalize_phone, DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE and _INDIAN_MOBILE_RE byte-identical.

Implement the marker branch per plan.md 1.3: trim, build a separator-tolerant `compact` with re.sub(r'[\s\-().]', '', text) which PRESERVES '+' and '00', branch on compact.startswith('+') then compact.startswith('00'), else raise MissingCountryCode. Only AFTER that branch call re.sub(r'\D','',rest). Never prepend DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE, never consult _INDIAN_MOBILE_RE.

Add the validation rules: reject a leading '0' in the remainder (no country code starts with zero); require 8 <= len(digits) <= 15; strip exactly ONE trunk zero only when digits starts '91' and the next digit is '0'. No trunk handling for any other country.

Write the docstring to the density of the surrounding module: state the reject decision for no-country-code input and the three reasons (handoff section 6, PhoneField always emits a dial code, MISSING_CODE copy already exists); state why a wrapper that calls normalize_phone and inspects the result CANNOT work; state the 91-only trunk rule and its documented consequence (+44 07911 123456 -> +4407911123456, which the provider rejects, which is a visible failure rather than a silent misdelivery); state the 00 reading with the 009330994400 -> +9330994400 example.

Write tests/test_phone_country_code_preservation.py covering plan.md 3.1 (the inverted reproduction table including the 00-prefix row, the 91-only trunk row, the non-India trunk row and the 00-reading row), 3.2 (a frozen byte-identical snapshot of normalize_phone over the full legacy case table, which must also record the legacy CORRUPTING outputs as documented legacy behaviour with a comment saying why the legacy value is retained for its 8 non-entry-point callers), 3.3 (no-country-code rejection, asserting isinstance of MissingCountryCode, InvalidPhoneNumber and ValueError), and 3.4 (the monkeypatch tripwire test on BOTH the '+' and the '00' input, plus the secondary AST-walk structural guard mirroring tests/test_payment_vocabulary_at_decision_points.py).

Wire amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/identity/registration.py: both begin() (~line 145) and complete() (~line 217) call normalize_phone_preserving_country instead of normalize_phone. Keep the `except customer_identity.InvalidPhoneNumber` clauses exactly as they are - MissingCountryCode subclasses it, which is why no control flow changes. Add a comment at each site naming the defect and why this door is strict while normalize_phone is not.

Migrate tests/test_registration.py and tests/test_customer_registration_handler.py per plan.md 1.5: PHONE becomes '+919330994400'; the '9000000001' literals at lines ~166, ~179, ~332 become '+919000000001'; test_every_spelling_reaches_one_counter keeps the three explicit-code spellings ('+919330994400', '0091 9330994400', '+91 93309 94400') and loses the two bare ones; ADD a new sibling test asserting the two bare spellings now return INVALID_PHONE and consume no throttle budget. Do not loosen any existing assertion.

Fix _normalise_phone at amplify/functions/auth/customer-whatsapp-auth/handler.py lines 172-179 IN PLACE, applying the same marker branch and returning digits only with no '+'. Keep it raising ValueError. Add a comment recording that the duplication is forced by standalone packaging (scripts/deploy_all_lambdas.py:174, deployed Layers is null) and naming normalize_phone_preserving_country as the canonical implementation. Verify the handler still imports nothing from lambda_utils - adding an import would break its live package.

Add the drift-agreement test from plan.md 3.5: for every row in the 3.1 table, assert trigger._normalise_phone(row) == module.normalize_phone_preserving_country(row).lstrip('+'). This is what keeps the two implementations from diverging given they cannot share code.

Add the remaining 3.5 wiring tests: begin() sends to exactly +6591234567 and never +916591234567; complete() passes +6591234567 to create_customer and provision_login (the identity-reservation proof); _mask_phone('+6591234567') ends 4567 and carries no 91 prefix.

Normalise the email-verification throttle axis at amplify/functions/auth/email-verification/handler.py line ~201: try normalize_phone_preserving_country(body.get('phone')) for the throttle subject, fall back to the normalised email when it raises, and NEVER return 400 on phone shape - the phone is optional on that endpoint. Add the test asserting '+65 9123 4567' and '+6591234567' produce one throttle subject and an unparseable phone falls back without a 400.

Add the plan.md 3.6 safety assertions: no new logging expression in the touched files interpolates a phone number, an OTP or a secret, not even reduced to a boolean or ternary; exception logging uses type(exc).__name__; no full phone number appears in any response body built by the touched handlers.

  normalize_phone, DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE and _INDIAN_MOBILE_RE are byte-identical: the diff for

DIVERGENCES FROM THE PLAN, both deliberate, with reasons:
  1. The trigger's length bound was widened from `10 <= len(digits) <= 15` to
     `8 <= len(digits) <= 15`, to match the canonical implementation. The plan said only
     'apply the marker branch'. Reason: a TIGHTER bound at sign-in than at the registration
     door is the same class of harm being fixed - a customer could register successfully with
     an 8 or 9 digit E.164 number and then be permanently unable to sign in. No existing test
     asserted the 10-digit floor, every test value is +919876543210, and the pool is
     AllowAdminCreateUserOnly so a wider accept opens nothing. Recorded in a comment at the
     site. Reviewer: if you disagree, reverting to 10 is a one-line change and the
     drift-agreement test still passes, because no row of the 3.1 table is under 10 digits.
  2. The plan's 3.4 secondary guard was specified as one AST test; it is implemented as TWO -
     test_the_strict_function_body_cannot_reach_the_india_default (no Call to normalize_phone,
     no DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE, no _INDIAN_MOBILE_RE) and
     test_the_marker_branch_precedes_every_digit_strip (statement-level ordering: the marker
     branch must come before any '\\D' strip). The second was added because the first does not
     actually catch the failure mode the plan cares about - a function could avoid all three
     forbidden symbols and still strip digits first.
     NOTE for anyone editing that test: it compares ast.unparse output per STATEMENT with the
     docstring excluded. An earlier version unparsed the whole FunctionDef and failed, because
     the docstring legitimately quotes re.sub(r'\\D', ...) while explaining the rule. Same
     reason tests/test_payment_vocabulary_at_decision_points.py walks the AST rather than grepping.
